## Starting and Choosing a Path

### 1. What does llmshieldr do?

It adds inspectable checks around prompts, retrieved context, conversations,
documents, tool calls, tool output, streams, and model responses. It also
provides policies, output contracts, grounding checks, budgets, audits,
telemetry, optional semantic review, and external-detector adapters.

### 2. Which function should a new application start with?

Use <code>secure_chat()</code> for a guarded end-to-end model call. Use
individual <code>scan_*()</code> functions when the application owns
orchestration or needs one boundary check.

### 3. Does scanning text require internet access?

Rules, local NLP checks, built-in recognizers, and policy construction run
locally. Network use occurs only when you choose a remote chat, reviewer,
Presidio service, OPA service, or another network-backed callback.

### 4. Which policy should I choose?

Choose the nearest domain preset, inspect its rules and controls, then measure
it on application data. <code>comprehensive</code> is broad and can create more
false positives. Policy names are starting configurations, not assurance or
compliance levels.

### 5. What is the baseline policy?

<code>baseline</code> is a compatibility alias for
<code>enterprise_default</code>.

### 6. What do allow, redact, and block mean?

They are scanner actions. Allow releases cleaned text, redact releases text
after configured span handling, and block prevents release. At orchestration
level, policy controls can map a block to <code>refuse</code> or
<code>escalate</code>.

## Providers and Credentials

### 7. How do I use Gemini?

Install <code>ellmer</code>, store <code>GEMINI_API_KEY</code> or
<code>GOOGLE_API_KEY</code> in <code>~/.Renviron</code>, restart R, and call
<code>secure_chat(provider = "gemini", model = "...")</code>.

### 8. Is the Gemini key read from the project?

It is read from the R process environment by the provider package. Keep the key
in a user-level <code>~/.Renviron</code> or a deployment secret manager. Do not
commit project credentials.

### 9. Is Gemini's free tier guaranteed?

No. Google controls account eligibility, model availability, quotas, regions,
pricing, and data-use terms. Check the current Gemini Developer API
documentation for the project and region.

### 10. How do I use Ollama?

Start Ollama, pull a model, and call
<code>secure_chat(provider = "ollama", model = "model-name")</code>. A default
local server normally needs no API key.

### 11. Can I use another provider?

Yes. Use a provider name understood by <code>ellmer::chat()</code>, pass
provider options through <code>provider_args</code>, or provide an existing
chat object or R callback.

### 12. Why are shield_gemini() and shield_ollama() deprecated?

The common <code>secure_chat(provider = ...)</code> path supports providers
without duplicating orchestration. The old wrappers still forward calls and
emit a standard deprecation warning.

### 13. Can the assistant and semantic reviewer use different providers?

Yes. Set <code>reviewer_provider</code>, <code>reviewer_model</code>, and
<code>reviewer_provider_args</code>, or supply a reviewer function or chat
object. Text may then be sent to a second service.

## Detection and Findings

### 14. What is the difference between rules, NLP, LLM, and both?

Rules are deterministic policy rules and configured scanners. NLP runs local
intent heuristics. LLM uses a supplied semantic reviewer. Both combines policy
rules with semantic review.

### 15. Why did a paraphrase pass a keyword rule?

Deterministic rules only recognize encoded evidence. Add domain vocabulary and
benign counterexamples, enable local NLP, or use a tested semantic reviewer.
Put the missed text into the evaluation corpus before changing behavior.

### 16. Can semantic review replace rules?

Treat it as another layer. Reviewer responses can vary, time out, fail schema
validation, or change with model updates. Keep deterministic controls for
stable requirements.

### 17. What happens if the reviewer fails?

The default is conservative and blocks. Configure
<code>policy_controls(on_reviewer_error = ...)</code> to block, escalate, or
continue with rules only. A fail-open choice needs monitoring and a documented
risk decision.

### 18. Why did one finding immediately block?

A critical finding or a rule with an explicit block action blocks regardless
of the aggregate threshold. Inspect <code>report$findings</code> and the policy
thresholds.

### 19. Is risk_score a probability?

No. It is a deterministic severity index from zero to one. Findings are
deduplicated, severity contributions are summed, and the score is capped at
one.

### 20. Why is report$tokens NULL?

Token reporting is opt-in. Set <code>show_tokens = TRUE</code>. Exact counts
depend on provider support; otherwise the package may attach an estimate or
leave the value unavailable.

### 21. Why did explain_findings() print?

Text format prints one set of console bullets and returns the character vector
invisibly. Assignment captures the value but does not suppress the intentional
console output.

### 22. What can I pass to explain_findings()?

Pass a complete <code>shieldr_report</code> or its list of findings. Markdown
and HTML formats return content for reports or interfaces.

### 23. Does the package find every PII, PHI, or secret?

No. Patterns and recognizers have false positives and false negatives. Add
domain recognizers, optional providers, and representative evaluation cases.
Minimize data before it reaches the guardrail whenever possible.

### 24. How do I support multiple languages?

Supply a language detector through <code>language_fn</code>, configure allowed
languages, add language-specific rules and recognizers, and evaluate each
language separately.

## Policies, Rules, and Redaction

### 25. Should a custom rule use a regex or a function?

Use regex for stable textual evidence and useful spans. Use a function for
structured parsing or multi-condition logic. Keep both implementations
bounded and test nearby benign language.

### 26. How do I avoid overblocking?

For every risky positive example, keep one or more close benign examples.
Narrow the stage and expression, compare policies on the same corpus, and
review every changed decision.

### 27. Does redaction change the source record?

No. It changes cleaned text in the report and orchestration path. Databases,
documents, logs, caches, and upstream systems need separate controls.

### 28. Is hash redaction anonymous?

No. Deterministic hashes link repeated values, and small source spaces can be
guessed. Treat them as sensitive pseudonymous metadata.

### 29. Why did a function rule not redact text?

Redaction needs character spans. A Boolean function finding can change the
action but cannot identify exact text to replace. Return one-based
<code>start</code> and <code>end</code> values for span-aware redaction.

## RAG, Documents, and URLs

### 30. Does context_policy() prevent cross-tenant retrieval?

It rejects rows before model submission, but the query must already enforce
tenant and ACL scope. This avoids retrieving unauthorized content in the first
place.

### 31. How should malicious retrieved text be handled?

Treat every row as untrusted, preserve its source, scan it separately, and
drop, block, refuse, or escalate according to policy. Instructions inside a
document must not override application authorization.

### 32. Can scan_document() read a PDF or image?

It scans text in a <code>document_input</code>. Use a sandboxed extraction
service for PDF, image, Office, and archive content, then preserve extraction,
OCR, hidden-text, checksum, and source metadata.

### 33. Do citations prove that an answer is true?

No. Grounding can require admitted source IDs and use a custom validator.
Citations alone do not prove source quality, entailment, current facts, or
absence of contradiction.

### 34. Does scan_url_target() stop SSRF by itself?

No. It validates supplied URL, IP, and redirect evidence without making a
request. DNS, redirect, connection, and egress enforcement belong in the HTTP
client and network layer.

## Tools, Output, and Streaming

### 35. Why are all tool calls denied?

The default empty allowlist denies tool-enabled chats. List approved names with
<code>allowed_tools</code> or use <code>tool_policy()</code>.

### 36. Does tool_policy() replace service authorization?

No. The downstream service must authorize identity, tenant, object ownership,
amount, and operation again at the point of execution.

### 37. Is JSON Schema enough to make tool input safe?

No. It validates shape and selected constraints. It does not make values safe
for SQL, shell, filesystem, network, or business use.

### 38. Can an output contract safely execute generated code?

No. It validates text or structure. Execute code, SQL, commands, templates, or
URLs only in separately designed sandboxes and destination controls.

### 39. Can streamed chunks be displayed before finish()?

That can expose unsafe output before the final decision. The conservative
<code>stream_guard()</code> buffers chunks and emits cleaned text after
<code>$finish()</code>.

### 40. Why does streaming add latency?

Safe release needs enough text to catch split payloads and a final whole-output
scan. That trades token-by-token display for a clear release boundary.

## Statistics, Audit, and Operations

### 41. How do I display time, tokens, and network information?

Set <code>show_stats = TRUE</code>. Statistics are messages and do not alter
the returned object.

### 42. Why are upload and download rates unavailable?

Many provider transports do not expose request and response byte counts.
The package reports unavailable instead of guessing wire traffic.

### 43. Why is network use unknown for my callback?

An arbitrary R function can use a network client without informing the
package. Add application telemetry around that client when exact evidence is
needed.

### 44. What does metadata-only audit remove?

It removes prompt and output text, finding excerpts, and reviewer details. It
retains actions, IDs, scores, timestamps, source references, and operational
metrics, which can still be sensitive.

### 45. How do I persist full audit content?

First request <code>audit_content = "full"</code> in
<code>secure_chat()</code>, then set
<code>include_content = TRUE</code> in <code>write_audit_log()</code>. Protect
the destination and define retention.

### 46. What is audit_key?

It is a secret HMAC key for fingerprints of omitted content. The key is not
stored. Load it from a secret manager and plan rotation because changing it
changes correlation values.

### 47. Does telemetry contain prompts?

Package telemetry events omit prompts, output, finding matches, and reviewer
excerpts. Review application-supplied attributes and exporter behavior too.

### 48. Does rate_guard() coordinate multiple machines?

The default backend is process-local. Optional file locking coordinates
workers on one machine. Multi-host deployments need an application-owned
shared atomic backend.

### 49. Does the OWASP crosswalk prove compliance?

No. It maps package controls to OWASP LLM Top 10 for 2026 categories.
Compliance and security depend on the complete system, evidence, operations,
and applicable requirements.

## Troubleshooting and Evaluation

### 50. Why did secure_chat() return no output?

Inspect <code>result$action</code> and its audit. Prompt, context, budget,
reviewer, tool, output, contract, or grounding controls may have stopped
release.

### 51. How should I fix a false positive?

Keep the benign example, identify the exact finding, narrow the rule or stage,
and rerun the complete case set. Avoid broad allowlists that suppress unrelated
risk.

### 52. How should I fix a false negative?

Add the missed input and variants to the evaluation set, add benign
counterexamples, then improve the rule, recognizer, NLP path, context control,
or reviewer.

### 53. How should I compare policy changes?

Use <code>compare_policies()</code> on a versioned case set and review every
changed action. Report malicious detection, sensitive redaction, benign false
positives, action accuracy, and latency.

### 54. Can package examples contact live services during CRAN checks?

They should not. Keep provider, network, executable, secret, and private-service
examples unevaluated. Routine examples and tests should be deterministic,
local, fast, and credential free.

### 55. What should a bug report include?

Include package and R versions, operating system, policy name and version,
check mode, a minimal sanitized input, expected and actual actions, and the
finding summary. Add provider and model names for provider issues. Never
publish credentials or private prompts.
